title: Ashtpadi 14, salok: give up cleverness
hook: taj siaanap: give up cleverness and remember the Lord (Sukhmani 14)

segments.voice: Yesterday, rasnaa, the tongue: it learns a taste for the Name or for faults, so guard it. Today, the fourteenth ashtpadi begins.

You're in the shower, rehearsing. If I say this to my boss, then she'll say that, and then I'll mention the other thing, and that way it looks like it was her idea. Version two. Version three. The water runs, the plan gets cleverer, and somewhere around version five you notice that you're not actually solving anything. You're just circling. The fourteenth ashtpadi of Sukhmani opens with a two-word instruction for exactly that state: taj siaanap. Give up the cleverness.
screen: `IN THE SHOWER, REHEARSING.` → `VERSION TWO. VERSION FIVE.` → `TAJ SIAANAP.`

segments.voice: Here's the salok, in paraphrase. Give up your cleverness, good people, and remember the Lord, the King. Keep in your mind hope in the One alone. Then, Nanak, pain, doubt and fear depart. Taj: give up, let go. Siaanap: cleverness, from siaanaa, a Punjabi word that can mean wise, but also shrewd, crafty, the one who always has an angle. The salok means that second sense. Careful, because this is easy to misread. Sukhmani isn't against thinking. Guru Nanak praised the person who reflects on learning, and Sikh history is full of scholars, poets and builders. Siaanap is narrower: the scheming mind, always calculating how to come out on top, how to arrange people, how to secure every outcome in advance. Why let it go? Look at what the salok promises instead. Three things depart: dookh, pain; bharam, doubt; and bhau, fear. That's precisely the list of what the scheming mind produces. The shower plan isn't really about the boss. It's fear, wearing a clever coat. The more angles you calculate, the more angles there are to fear. The salok's alternative is simple to say and hard to do: ek aas, one hope, kept in the mind. Not a dozen backup plans, each with its own worry attached. One place to rest. The next stanzas turn to where that hope should and shouldn't rest. Today, only the first move: put the clever plan down.
screen: `TAJ: LET GO. SIAANAP: CLEVERNESS.` · `NOT THINKING, BUT SCHEMING.` · `PAIN, DOUBT AND FEAR DEPART.` · `EK AAS: ONE HOPE.` · then, large: `DROP THE CLEVERNESS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a plan you've been circling, a conversation you keep rehearsing, an outcome you're trying to arrange, and see all its versions clearly. Then, on an out-breath, set it down; you can still act tomorrow, you're only putting down the circling. Rest in one simple hope instead of ten clever angles, and if you pray, say Waheguru on the out-breath.
Siaanap, cleverness, shrewdness. The salok says: give it up, keep one hope, and pain, doubt and fear depart.
Your line: drop the cleverness. One hope is lighter than ten angles. Four hundred ninety days now.

howItsDone: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib open the fourteenth ashtpadi with the salok beginning taj siaanap, give up cleverness, and many read it as a turn from scheming toward a single hope in God.

original.note: Gurmukhi: siaanap, cleverness, shrewdness, from siaanaa, clever or wise.

trapdoor: what you thought: give up cleverness means don't be smart.
what it means: put down the scheming, angle-calculating mind and rest in one hope.
what a scholar hears: siaanaa covers both wise and crafty in Punjabi; the salok pairs giving it up with ek aas, one hope, and names three results, dookh, bharam, bhau.
guess: cleverness that schemes for an angle
wisdom gained from years of study
doubt about whether God is real

chat.says: Sukhmani says give up cleverness. So are Sikhs against thinking hard?
options: No. Siaanap is the scheming mind working angles; Guru Nanak praised reflecting on learning.
Yes, Sikhs value simple faith over study, so scholars and deep thinkers miss the point.
It means never planning ahead at all; any plan for the future goes against the salok.
chat.meaning: Siaanap here means shrewd scheming, not thought; the salok says give it up, keep one hope, and pain, doubt and fear depart.

ek aas.meaning: one hope, kept in the mind
